title: Microburst cost-latency lab notes & wireframe synthesis
content:
PURPOSE:
Quick synthesis from the microburst investigation (short high-concurrency spikes) and a first-pass wireframe idea set for a microburst-aware cost+latency console lens. Goal: give engineers and product owners a compact view to surface transient cost spikes and the per-token latency contributors during bursts, and to make mitigation actions discoverable (cache warm, route, throttle, degrade model).

BACKGROUND / PROBLEM STATEMENT:
- Customers see occasional short-lived bill/latency spikes that are hard to reason about in current token breakdown views.
- Existing token inspector assumes steady-state averages; bursts distort aggregation and hide marginal token cost during tail latency.
- Need a minimal lens that explains: where burst originated (route/model/route params), how many tokens marginally increased cost, and what latency component spiked (serving queue, kernel, KV cache miss).

HIGH-LEVEL USER JOBS:
- SRE: detect and triage burst source quickly (first 2 minutes).
- Eng: reproduce burst pattern and tune batching/buffer.
- Product/CS: explain to customer and recommend config changes.

OBSERVATIONS FROM TRACES (sampled):
- Typical microburst length: 10s-90s; 20% of bursts < 15s.
- KV cache-miss rate jumps correlate with first 5s of bursts -> heavy cold-cache cost.
- Batching efficiency drops during high concurrency -> per-token unit cost up 1.4x.
- Some bursts map to specific prompt templates (large system prompts + user loops).

WIREFRAME CONCEPTS (sketch descriptions) - aim for single-pane microburst lens
1) Burst Timeline (top strip): compact sparkline with mini-histogram of requests/sec; hover to show 5s window details (requests, avg latency, total tokens, cost delta).
2) Burst Map (left column): small stacked bars by route/model showing contribution to request volume during selected window; click-to-filter to open token-level view.
3) Marginal Token Waterfall (center): waterfall showing cost delta broken down by token-class (system/prompt/user/response continuation) and by backend component (serving compute, KV fetches, network). Each bar annotated with token count and microsecs/token.
4) Latency Slice Heat-strip (right): per-token latency heat-strip (sequence index vs p99/p50) for the selected invocation samples. Highlight large jumps and mark likely root cause (cache-miss, scheduling).
5) Quick Actions Footer: warm-cache (synthetic prefix), pin fallback-model, enable transient rate-limit, capture full trace to S3.

INTERACTIONS / MICROCOPY NOTES:
- Hover on waterfall: "Delta cost: $0.018 (vs baseline). 32% of delta from cold KV fetches."
- Burst badge: small red dot + tooltip "Microburst: 23s; peak 420 rps"
- CTA when model pinned: "Pin model variant to stable-quantized to reduce burst cost"

DATA & INSTRUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS:
- 5s-resolution aggregates for RPS and token counts (for UI responsiveness).
- Sampled invocation traces (1%?) with full per-token timings retained for selected windows.
- Derived fields: marginal_cost_delta, kv_miss_rate_window, avg_batch_size_window.
- Analytics events: console.microburst.view, console.microburst.action.warm_cache, console.microburst.pin_model (include burst_id).

ACCESSIBILITY / PERFORMANCE CONSTRAINTS:
- Default to lightweight aggregated views; only fetch heavy per-token traces when user clicks "Inspect window".
- Keyboard accessible timeline scrubbing and list of quick actions.

BACKLOG (proposed priorities)
MVP (P0, 2-week sprint):
- UI: timeline strip + stacked route map + marginal token waterfall (static mock). Owner: Liam.
- API: 5s-resolution aggregation endpoint + burst detection flag. Owner: Aaron.
- Data: store burst_id with sampled traces. Owner: Sofia.
- Acceptance: load a real burst in demo project and show cost delta and suggested quick action.

M1 (P1, next sprint):
- Per-token heat-strip and root-cause annotations (KV miss / batch drop).
- Quick action implementations (warm-cache proto + pin model).
- Analytics and instrumentation hardened.

M2 (P2):
- Simulation tool to replay bursts in staging for cost regression tests.
- Auto-suggestions (ml-driven) for optimal model variant and batching config.

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS:
- Sampling rate tradeoff: 1% traces might miss short microbursts; storing many traces is expensive. Need retention policy and egress cost calc.
- How to compute "baseline" for delta during non-stationary workloads? Rolling baseline vs historical median?
- Ownership: is this product-console or infra-observability surface? (ask PMs)

NEXT STEPS:
- Run quick design crit with eng + SRE (target: 2025-01-20).
- Wireframe clickable prototype in Figma (Liam) + link to demo dataset.
- Create JIRA epic INFR-1427 with subtasks for API, data, UI.

NOTES TO SELF:
- Keep visuals compact — customers will look at the console in incident context on small screens.
- Consider a "burst severity" ordinal (low/med/high) for quick sorting in incident manager.

SAMPLE MOCK DATA SNIPPET (for devs):
- window_start: 2025-01-09T18:42:10Z; rps_peak=412; tokens_total=73_412; cost_delta=$1.27; kv_miss_rate=0.34; avg_batch_size=1.6

REFERENCES / LINKS:
- Slack thread: #prod-costs "microburst pattern discussion" (link pinned in JIRA).
- Existing explorer: token-chronicle (note: not burst-aware).

END.
